name: Exa
description: Exa neural + keyword web search built for AI — semantic search by meaning, returning ranked results (title/url/score) with optional page text. Defaults to the first-party api.exa.ai; also available via the BlockRun and StableEnrich aggregator gateways. Keyless pay-per-call x402. (For synthesized answers with citations, see Exa Answer.)

numResults.description: Number of results to return (max 10 for x402)

type.description: Search type: auto, keyword, neural, deep-lite, deep, deep-reasoning

contents.description: Content fields to include: text, highlights, summary

query.description: Free-text web search query (passed as ?query=... GET param).

usage.callShape: POST https://api.exa.ai/search with JSON body {query} (optionally numResults, type:'neural'|'keyword'|'auto', category). Returns body.results[].

inputExample.query: latest research on AI agent memory

usage.outputShape: body.results[].{id,title,url,publishedDate,author,score}; body.requestId. (Add {"contents":{"text":true}} to also get body.results[].text page content.)
quirks: Required field is `query` (a search phrase or natural-language description). Optional: numResults (default ~10), type ('neural'|'keyword'|'auto'), category, includeDomains/excludeDomains, startPublishedDate.
This is the SEARCH endpoint → returns ranked results[] (id/title/url/score), NOT a synthesized answer. For a direct answer-with-citations use the Exa Answer service instead.

DEFAULT provider is the first-party api.exa.ai/search (~$0.007). Aggregator routes blockrun.ai/api/v1/exa/search and stableenrich.dev/api/exa/search (~$0.01) are also available — pin one with backendProviderId 'blockrun' or 'stableenrich'. All take {query} and return the same results[] shape. api.exa.ai re-verified working 2026-06-10 (200).
To fetch full page text in one call, pass {"contents":{"text":true}}; results[].text is then populated (may raise the price).
usage.guide: POST https://api.exa.ai/search (first-party, the default) with a JSON body {"query":"<search phrase>", "numResults":5}. It is keyless x402 (~$0.007 USDC on Base — no API key). The response is synchronous JSON: read body.results[] (each has title, url, publishedDate, score). To also pull page text, add {"contents":{"text":true}}. For a synthesized answer with citations instead of raw results, use the Exa Answer service.

name: Exa Contents
description: Exa content retrieval — fetch the cleaned page text (and highlights/summary) for one or more URLs. Defaults to the first-party api.exa.ai; also via BlockRun and StableEnrich. Keyless pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.exa.ai/contents with JSON body {urls:["<url>",...], text:true} (or {ids:[...]}). Returns body.results[] with page text.
usage.outputShape: body.results[].{id,title,url,author,text}; body.requestId. text holds the cleaned page content. Optionally request highlights/summary too.
quirks: Required field is `urls` (an array of page URLs) — NOT `query`. You can also pass `ids` (Exa result ids). Pass text:true (and optionally highlights/summary:true) to choose what content comes back.
Pricing is per page per content type (~$0.001 each on first-party) — fetching many urls or multiple content types scales the cost.

DEFAULT provider is first-party api.exa.ai/contents (~$0.001). Aggregator routes blockrun.ai/api/v1/exa/contents and stableenrich.dev/api/exa/contents (~$0.002) also available via backendProviderId. api.exa.ai re-verified working 2026-06-10 (200, returned results[].text).
usage.guide: POST https://api.exa.ai/contents (first-party, the default) with a JSON body {"urls":["<page url>"],"text":true}. Keyless x402 (~$0.001 per page on Base). The response is synchronous JSON: read body.results[].text for the cleaned page content. Use this to pull the full text of pages you already have URLs for (e.g. from an Exa Search result).

name: Exa Answer
description: Exa Answer — ask a natural-language question and get a synthesized, cited answer (not raw search results), powered by Exa neural search over the live web. Keyless pay-per-call x402 via the BlockRun and StableEnrich gateways.

usage.callShape: POST https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/exa/answer with JSON body {query}

inputExample.query: What is the capital of France?

usage.outputShape: body.answer (synthesized answer string with inline [n] citation markers); body.citations[].{title,url,publishedDate,image,favicon}; body.costDollars.total; body.requestId
quirks: Required field is `query` (a natural-language question). Returns a synthesized answer, NOT raw results — for ranked search results use the Exa Search service instead.
Answer text contains inline [1][2] citation markers that index into body.citations[]
No first-party api.exa.ai/answer endpoint is published, so this is served via the BlockRun (default) and StableEnrich aggregators (~$0.01). Pin with backendProviderId 'stableenrich' if desired.
Keyless x402 (~$0.01 USDC on Base). BlockRun route re-verified working 2026-06-10 (200, returned answer + citations).
usage.guide: POST https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/exa/answer with a JSON body {"query": "<your natural-language question>"}. Keyless x402, ~$0.01 USDC on Base. The response is synchronous: read body.answer for the synthesized answer (with inline [n] markers) and body.citations[] for the supporting sources (title + url). Use this for direct factual answers with citations rather than raw search results.

name: Exa Find Similar
description: Exa find-similar — give a URL and get semantically similar pages from across the web. Served via the BlockRun and StableEnrich gateways. Keyless pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/exa/find-similar with JSON body {url}
usage.outputShape: body.results[].{id,title,url,author,score}; body.requestId. Each result is a page similar to the input url, with a relevance score.
quirks: Required field is `url` (a single page URL) — NOT `query`. Returns pages semantically similar to that url.

No first-party api.exa.ai find-similar endpoint is published here, so this is served via the BlockRun (default) and StableEnrich aggregators (~$0.01). Pin with backendProviderId 'stableenrich' if desired.
Keyless x402 (~$0.01 USDC on Base). BlockRun route re-verified working 2026-06-10 (200, returned scored results[]).
usage.guide: POST https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/exa/find-similar with a JSON body {"url": "<a page url>"}. Keyless x402 (~$0.01 USDC on Base). The response is synchronous JSON: read body.results[] (each has title, url, and a similarity score). Use this to discover pages related to one you already have.

name: Scout Academic Search
description: Academic literature search — Semantic Scholar and arXiv paper discovery with metadata and abstracts. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: GET https://scout.hugen.tokyo/scout/arxiv?q=<query>&per_page=<n>&sort=<relevance|date>&category=<arxiv_cat> (only q is required; all params are query-string, no body)
usage.outputShape: body.data[] is the array of papers, each with .id, .title, .summary (abstract), .authors[], .url, .pdf_url, .categories[], .date, .updated. body.count = number returned, body.source = "arxiv", body.query echoes the query, body.success = true.
usage.guide: Search arXiv for academic papers via a plain GET with x402 payment ($0.01 USDC on Base). Put your search terms in the required `q` query param; optionally add `per_page` (1-50, default 10), `sort` (relevance|date), and `category` (e.g. cs.AI). Read results from body.data[] — each item gives title, summary (abstract), authors, the arxiv abstract url and pdf_url. body.count tells you how many came back. Synchronous, no auth, no polling.

name: MemoryAPI
description: Persistent agent memory with semantic retrieval and tools — store and recall context across sessions via vector search. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.memoryapi.org/x402/memory?query=<text>&agent_id=<your-agent-id>&limit=<n>
usage.outputShape: body.success (bool), body.results[] (matched memory items), body.count (int)
quirks: query and agent_id are BOTH required query-string params; omitting either will likely 4xx
Results are scoped per agent_id — a fresh/unknown agent_id returns {success:true,results:[],count:0}. You must have stored memories under that same agent_id first to get hits.
This is the semantic-retrieval (read) endpoint only; it does not store memories.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.memoryapi.org/x402/memory with required query params query (natural-language search) and agent_id (your stable agent identifier), plus optional limit (default 5). Pay $0.001 USDC on Base via x402. The response is JSON: read body.results[] for the matched memory items and body.count for how many were returned. Use the same agent_id you stored memories under, otherwise results will be empty.

name: Honcho Agent Memory
description: Honcho is persistent memory + reasoning for AI agents: store every conversation turn, then query a peer's memory in natural language and get reasoned context back — not a similarity search over chunks. It continuously builds a representation of each user/peer (markdown summary + fact card) and can return LLM-ready session context. Keyless pay-per-call over x402: storing messages is $2/1M tokens ($0.001 floor), memory queries are $0.001–$0.50 by reasoning depth, and all reads (search, context, representations, cards, session/peer listing) are free with a SIWX wallet identity. Each wallet owns a private workspace.

operations.name: Store Messages

peer.description: Peer ID for the author of this message.

metadata.description: Optional key-value metadata for this message.

operations.instructions: Append conversation messages to a session; auto-provisions the session and each authoring peer on first use. Call this after every turn so Honcho can learn. Dynamic price: $2 / 1M tokens (≈chars/4), $0.001 floor, $5 ceiling.

usage.callShape: POST https://agentcash.honcho.dev/api/honcho/messages with JSON body {session, messages:[{peer, content, metadata?}]} (x402 payment; workspace = payer wallet)

messages.content: Got it — I'll keep it short.

usage.outputShape: body.messages[] — each stored message with {id, content, peer_id, session_id, created_at, token_count}
quirks: PAID via x402 on Base (USDC). Dynamic price: $2 / 1M tokens estimated as ceil(total_chars/4), $0.001 floor, $5 ceiling. A short 2-message turn settles at the $0.001 floor (verified).
Auto-provisions: never pass a workspace field. The session and every authoring peer are created on first reference — no explicit create call.
Workspace is keyed to the PAYER wallet. Reuse the same wallet for the SIWX read endpoints so stores and reads share one private workspace.
Also advertises MPP (Tempo); the registry keeps the x402 route only.
usage.guide: POST /api/honcho/messages with {"session":"<id>","messages":[{"peer":"<user>","content":"..."},{"peer":"Assistant","content":"..."}]}. Keyless x402 on Base — a short turn costs the $0.001 floor. The session and peers auto-provision; reuse the session id for the rest of the conversation. Read back the stored rows from body.messages[].

operations.name: Query Memory (Chat)

peer.description: Peer ID — a stable identifier for a participant (agent, user, assistant).

query.description: Natural language question to ask about this peer's memory.

session.description: Scope the query to a session.

target.description: Target peer ID — if set, queries what the peer knows about the target rather than its global memory.

reasoning_level.description: Reasoning depth (determines price). minimal=$0.001 (basic conclusions, instant), low=$0.01 (efficient synthesis, instant), medium=$0.05 (steerable reasoning, fast), high=$0.10 (deep synthesis, async), max=$0.50 (research-grade, async). Defaults to "low".

operations.instructions: Ask a natural-language question about a peer's memory; Honcho's reasoning system answers from everything learned across that peer's conversations. Price = reasoning_level: minimal $0.001, low $0.01 (default), medium $0.05, high $0.10, max $0.50. high/max are async.

usage.callShape: POST https://agentcash.honcho.dev/api/honcho/chat with JSON body {peer, query, session?, target?, reasoning_level?} (x402 payment)

inputExample.query: What communication style does this user prefer and what are their interests?

usage.outputShape: body.content — a natural-language answer string (may be null if nothing learned yet)
quirks: PAID via x402 on Base. Price is set by reasoning_level: minimal $0.001, low $0.01 (default), medium $0.05, high $0.10, max $0.50. Verified 'low' = $0.01.
high and max run ASYNCHRONOUSLY (deep synthesis); minimal/low/medium return inline.
Answers from Honcho's reasoning over stored messages — it works even before the peer's representation/card have been generated (verified: returned an accurate synthesis moments after storing).
Set `target` to ask what `peer` knows about another peer; omit `session` to query the peer's global memory.
usage.guide: POST /api/honcho/chat with {"peer":"<id>","query":"<question>"} and optionally session/target/reasoning_level. Keyless x402 on Base; default reasoning_level 'low' costs $0.01. Read the answer from body.content. Use the lowest reasoning_level that fits — minimal ($0.001) for quick reads, max ($0.50) for research-grade synthesis.

limit.description: Max number of results. Default 10, max 100.

session.description: Restrict search to a specific session.

peer.description: Restrict search to messages authored by a peer.

usage.outputShape: body.messages[] — matching messages {id, content, peer_id, session_id, created_at, token_count}; empty array when nothing matches

Scoped to the calling wallet's private workspace; a fresh wallet returns {messages:[]}.
Only `query` is required. Optional: limit (default 10, max 100), session, peer.
usage.guide: POST /api/honcho/search with {"query":"..."} and a SIWX identity (free, no payment). Optionally add limit/session/peer to narrow. Results are in body.messages[]; an empty array just means no stored memory matched for that wallet.

usage.callShape: POST https://agentcash.honcho.dev/api/honcho/<op> with JSON body. Paid ops (messages, chat) use x402 on Base; all other ops are free with a SIWX wallet identity.

messages.content: I prefer concise answers and love hiking.

usage.outputShape: Per-op JSON — messages[] for store/search/list, body.content for chat, {representation} / {peer_card} / {messages,summary,...} for the reads.
quirks: One wallet = one private workspace. Paid endpoints derive the workspace from the PAYER wallet; SIWX endpoints from the SIGNING wallet. Use the same wallet for paid stores and SIWX reads so they share one workspace. Never send a workspace field.
Auto-provisioning: sessions and peers are created on first reference (by /messages or /sessions/peers/add). There is no explicit create call.

representation, card, and session summaries are generated ASYNCHRONOUSLY by Honcho's reasoning — they return empty string / null immediately after a store (verified) and fill in later. This is expected, not an error.
chat DOES reason over freshly-stored messages even before representation/card exist (verified: an accurate synthesis returned seconds after storing).
Paid ops advertise both x402 and MPP (Tempo); only the x402 route is used here. The 402 challenge is a standard, decodable x402 v2 payload (this resolved the earlier 'no decodable accepts' block).
usage.guide: Memory loop: (1) after each turn, POST /api/honcho/messages with {session, messages:[{peer,content}...]} — keyless x402 on Base, ~$0.001 for a short turn; it auto-creates the session and peers. (2) When personalization helps, POST /api/honcho/chat with {peer, query, reasoning_level} to get a reasoned answer from that peer's memory ($0.001–$0.50 by depth; 'low' $0.01 default). (3) Reads are free with a SIWX identity: /search (semantic), /context (LLM-ready bundle), /representation and /card (learned profile — async, may be empty at first), and the /sessions + /peers listings. Reuse one wallet so everything lands in the same private workspace.

name: DYOR Knowledge Graph
description: Semantic search over the DYOR crypto knowledge graph — entity- and relationship-aware retrieval. Pay-per-call x402.

query.description: Entity name or semantic search query

entity_types.description: Filter by type: Token, Protocol, Chain, Organization, Person, Exchange, Pool

usage.outputShape: body.results[] (each: .uri, .name, .labels[], .similarity, .description); body.status, body.query, body.total_count
quirks: GET endpoint — params go in the query string, not a JSON body (query is required; optional limit, entity_types).
usage.guide: Call GET https://kg.dyor.network/api/search with a required `query` query-string param (entity name or semantic search query), optional `limit` (default 10) and `entity_types[]` filter (Token, Protocol, Chain, Organization, Person, Exchange, Pool). Pay $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base. The response is a plain synchronous JSON object; read the matched entities from body.results[], each having uri, name, similarity, and a description.

name: Semagram
description: Semagram semantic search — meaning-based retrieval over indexed content. Pay-per-call x402.

parameters.description: Maximum number of results. Price scales with limit (ceil(limit/100) * base price).
parameters.name: limit

usage.outputShape: body is a JSON array of objects; each: body[].uuid, body[].username, body[].name, body[].kind, body[].bio, body[].avatar_url, body[].user_count

All inputs are URL query params on a GET (q, limit, lang, kind, min_users, max_users) — no JSON body. Only q is required.
kind filter is restricted to enum: channel | group | bot.
usage.guide: Call GET https://semagram.io/api/agent/search with query params; only q (the search query string) is required. Optionally add limit (1-1000, default 100; price = ceil(limit/100) * $0.01, so keep limit<=100 for $0.01), lang (ISO 639-1), kind (channel/group/bot), min_users, max_users. Pay $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base. The response is a JSON array of matching Telegram entities; read body[].name, body[].username, body[].user_count, and body[].bio for each result.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/knowledge/wikidata?q=<search term> (x402 paid, ~$0.005 on Base). NOTE: registry lists POST but POST 404s — must use GET with a q query param.
usage.outputShape: body.results[] (each: .id Wikidata QID, .label, .description, .concept_uri, .url, .match); also body.query, body.lang, body.count

No request body; this is a GET endpoint.
Response includes a top-level _hint promo string that can be ignored.
Returns up to 10 entity matches ranked by label match.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.x402node.dev/knowledge/wikidata?q=<your search term> with x402 payment (~$0.005 USDC on Base). Do NOT use POST — it 404s. Read results from body.results[], where each item has .id (the Wikidata QID like Q937), .label, .description, and .concept_uri. Use body.results[0].id to grab the top entity match.

name: 2s Wikidata Entity
description: Fetch a single Wikidata entity by its ID (Q/P/M/L/S) and get the full structured knowledge-graph record — labels, descriptions, aliases (per language), claims/statements grouped by property, and Wikipedia sitelinks — across 110M+ CC0 public-domain entities.

id.description: Wikidata entity ID (Q42, P31, M..., L..., S...). Required.

languages.description: Comma-separated language codes controlling which label/description/alias strings are returned (default "en").

includeClaims.description: Whether to return claims/statements. Default true.

maxClaimsPerProperty.description: Cap on how many statements are returned per property.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/wikidata/entity?id={QID} (x402 paid, no request body). Optional query params: languages (comma-separated codes, default en), includeClaims (bool, default true), maxClaimsPerProperty (1-50, default 10).
usage.outputShape: body.data.items[] (array; one item for the requested id). Each item: .id (QID), .type, .pageId, .lastModified, .labels{lang:{language,value}}, .descriptions{lang:{...}}, .aliases{lang:[{...}]}, .claimsCount, .claims{propertyId:[{rank,type,valueType,value}]} (e.g. P31 instance-of), .sitelinksCount, .sitelinks{site:{site,title,url}}. body.data.ok, body.data.total, body.data.source{provider,url,license}. Settlement/cost echoed at body.meta{endpoint,cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.
quirks: Result is nested under body.data.items[] (an array even for a single id) — read items[0]; NOT the top-level {ok,total,items} shown in the 402 bazaar example.
id is a query-string param, not a path segment.

Observed: calling with only ?id=Q42 (no languages param) returned labels:{} and aliases:{} empty while descriptions.en was populated — pass languages=en (or your codes) explicitly to reliably populate labels/aliases.
sitelinks[site].url can be null even when title is present.
Provider offers a free trial: append ?trial=1 (or header X-2s-Trial:1) for one free real call per endpoint per hour (not used for the registry price).
usage.guide: Call GET https://2s.io/api/wikidata/entity with a required query param id set to a Wikidata entity ID (e.g. ?id=Q42 for Douglas Adams; also accepts P.../M.../L.../S... IDs). It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.0012 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key, no signup — the pay layer handles the 402. Optionally add languages=en,es to pick which language strings come back (recommended — without it labels/aliases may be empty), includeClaims=false to skip statements, and maxClaimsPerProperty=N (1-50) to cap statements per property. The response is synchronous JSON: read the entity from body.data.items[0] — .labels/.descriptions/.aliases for names, .claims{P31:[...]} for property statements (P31 = instance-of, etc.), and .sitelinks for Wikipedia article titles. Source is Wikidata (CC0 public domain).

name: Agentstools Scholar Citations
description: Citation graph for a single paper — resolve it by DOI, arXiv, PubMed, OpenAlex id or title and get both the works it references and the works that cite it (ranked, with ids, authors, venue, year and citation counts) from OpenAlex. Pay-per-call x402.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params (supply exactly ONE identifier; all optional in the schema but one is required to resolve a paper): doi (string — DOI, with or without a doi.org prefix), arxiv (string — arXiv id such as 2401.01234), pmid (string — PubMed id, digits), pmcid (string — PubMed Central id such as PMC1234567), openalex_id (string — OpenAlex work id such as W2741809807), title (string — paper title to resolve by search), id (string — any single identifier, type auto-detected), limit (integer 1-50, default 10 — max items returned per direction). No request body.
backends.outputSchema: { found (bool), work: { ids: {doi?,openalex?,pmid?,mag?}, title, year }, references: { total (int — full outgoing bibliography size), returned (int — capped by limit), items[]: { ids:{doi?,openalex?,pmid?}, title, authors[], venue, year, type, cited_by_count, is_oa, oa_pdf_url } }, citing: { total (int — full incoming citation count), returned (int), items[]: (same shape as references.items) }, influential_citation_count (int|null — from Semantic Scholar; null when that source is unavailable), sources: { used[] (e.g. ['openalex','semanticscholar']), partial (bool), errors? {<source>:<message>} }, disclaimer (string), attribution[] (string) }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/scholar/citations?doi=10.1038/nature14539&limit=10 (supply exactly ONE identifier — doi | arxiv | pmid | pmcid | openalex_id | title | id — plus optional limit 1-50; all query-string params, no request body)
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. body.found tells you whether the paper resolved; body.work gives the resolved paper's ids/title/year. body.references.total is the full size of the paper's outgoing bibliography and body.references.items[] is the capped page (limit items) of works it cites; body.citing.total is the full incoming citation count and body.citing.items[] is the capped page of works that cite it. Each item is {ids, title, authors[], venue, year, type, cited_by_count, is_oa, oa_pdf_url}, ranked by cited_by_count. body.influential_citation_count comes from Semantic Scholar (null if that source is unavailable). body.sources.used[] lists the registries fused and body.sources.partial=true (with body.sources.errors) flags a rate-limited/unavailable upstream — still a 200, never a 500.
quirks: Supply exactly ONE identifier — doi, arxiv, pmid, pmcid, openalex_id, title, or the auto-detected id — as a query param; limit (1-50, default 10) caps items per direction. No request body.

The citation graph is sourced from OpenAlex; influential_citation_count comes from Semantic Scholar and is null when that upstream is unavailable. On the verified call semanticscholar returned HTTP 403, so influential_citation_count was null and sources.partial was true — this is reported gracefully, never a 500.
Metadata only — returns links to legally-hosted open-access copies (oa_pdf_url when is_oa) but never rehosts restricted full-text.
Price $0.02 USDC on Base (eip155:8453); no API key.
usage.guide: Walk the citation graph around a single paper for literature review, prior-art search and bibliometric analysis. name: Agentstools Open-Access Locator
description: Given a DOI, finds whether a free, legally-hosted open-access copy of the paper exists (via Unpaywall with OpenAlex fallback) and returns the best PDF/landing-page link with its license, version and host type. Pay-per-call x402.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params: doi (string, REQUIRED in practice — a DOI with or without a doi.org prefix, e.g. '10.1038/nature14539'), id (string, optional alias for doi). No request body.
backends.outputSchema: { found (boolean), query: { doi (string, echoed) }, title (string), is_oa (boolean), best_oa: { is_oa (boolean), pdf_url (string|null — direct PDF link when available), landing_page (string — open-access landing page), license (string, e.g. 'cc-by','other-oa'), version (string — 'publishedVersion'|'acceptedVersion'|'submittedVersion'), host_type (string — 'repository'|'publisher'), source (string, e.g. 'unpaywall') }, sources: { partial (boolean), used (string[] — e.g. ['unpaywall','openalex']), errors (object) }, disclaimer (string), attribution (string[]) }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/scholar/oa?doi=10.1038/nature14539 (doi passed as a query-string param — 'id' is an accepted alias; no request body)
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. body.found is a boolean; body.title is the paper title; body.is_oa is whether an open-access copy exists; body.best_oa is the best location object {is_oa, pdf_url (may be null even when is_oa is true — see quirks), landing_page, license, version, host_type, source}; body.sources.used lists which registries answered (unpaywall/openalex) and sources.partial flags a degraded (one-source-down) response; attribution[] carries the required Unpaywall/OpenAlex credit. On a DOI with no open-access copy, found/is_oa are false and best_oa is empty/null — still a valid 200.

pdf_url can be null even when is_oa is true — the source (e.g. HAL/a repository) may only expose a landing_page, not a direct PDF; fall back to best_oa.landing_page in that case.
It never proxies, rehosts, or unlocks paywalled full-text — it only returns links the upstream registries point at; for restricted papers it returns found/is_oa false rather than a link.
sources.partial:true means one upstream (Unpaywall or OpenAlex) was unavailable and the answer is degraded, not failed — the response is still HTTP 200.
Attribution to Unpaywall (and OpenAlex CC0) is included in body.attribution as required by those sources.
Fixed price $0.008 USDC on Base (eip155:8453); no API key. Use this when you already have a DOI and only need the free copy — the heavier /scholar/paper fusion is a separate op.
usage.guide: Find a free, legally-hosted open-access copy of a paper when you already have its DOI. Note pdf_url can be null even when is_oa is true (some repositories only expose a landing page) — fall back to best_oa.landing_page. body.sources.used lists which registries answered and sources.partial flags a degraded one-source-down answer (still HTTP 200). It never rehosts or unlocks paywalled text; for restricted papers found/is_oa come back false. Required Unpaywall/OpenAlex attribution is in body.attribution. It is an x402 paid endpoint at a fixed $0.008 USDC on Base; no API key. Verified 2026-07-30 with doi='10.1038/nature14539' (the 'Deep learning' Nature paper) -> HTTP 200, found:true, is_oa:true, best_oa.landing_page https://hal.science/hal-04206682 (license other-oa, submittedVersion, repository, source unpaywall), $0.008 charged (tx 0xed6232b87234d8882399dfce86ea1d2e43bbccfdbd4d6da6d6be0e765930749e).

name: Agentstools Scholar Paper

inputSchema.description: Supply exactly one identifier (all params are query-string, no body).

doi.description: DOI, with or without a doi.org prefix (e.g. 10.1038/nature14539).

openalex_id.description: OpenAlex work id such as W2741809807.

title.description: Paper title to resolve by search.

id.description: Any single identifier; its type is auto-detected.

query.description: Echo of the resolved identifier {type, value}.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/scholar/paper?doi={doi} (or ?arxiv= / ?pmid= / ?pmcid= / ?openalex_id= / ?title= / ?id=) — x402 paid, no request body; supply exactly ONE identifier as a query param
usage.outputShape: Top-level fused JSON: found (bool), query {type,value}, ids crosswalk {doi,openalex,pmid,mag,...}, title, authors[] each {name, orcid, affiliations[]{name,ror}}, venue {name,type,issn,publisher}, year, type, concepts[], topics[], counts {cited_by:{openalex,crossref}, references:{openalex,crossref}, influential_citations?}, open_access {is_oa,pdf_url,landing_page,license,version,host_type}, provenance (per-field source map), sources {used[],partial,errors}, attribution[]. All inputs are query-string params — there is no request body despite it being a paid GET

The call never 500s on a missing/rate-limited/unconfigured source: those fields are omitted and the source is listed under sources.errors with sources.partial=true (in this run semanticscholar returned HTTP 403 so influential_citations was absent and partial=true)

open_access.pdf_url can be null even when is_oa=true — a landing_page (repository/publisher page) may be given instead of a direct PDF; it links the copy the source points at and never rehosts restricted full-text
authors[].orcid can be null; affiliations carry ROR ids when OpenAlex has them

name: Agentstools Docs Library
description: Returns up-to-date, version-pinned documentation for a library or API for coding agents — package identity (latest/requested version, license, repo, homepage, doc URLs, version list) plus the README or llms.txt section matching a topic, each with a provenance citation. Keyless PyPI, npm, crates and GitHub sources.

Required: ecosystem (string enum: npm | pypi | crates | github; aliases accepted — pip/python->pypi, cargo/rust->crates, node->npm, gh->github), name (string — package name; for github pass owner/repo such as coinbase/x402; npm scoped names @scope/name allowed). Check `found`, then read `identity` (ecosystem, name, latest_version, requested_version, resolved_version, license, repository, homepage, documentation, source, versions[], versions_count) and `doc` — the single README/llms.txt slice: heading, matched_topic (whether your topic matched a heading or it fell back to the intro), content (markdown, byte-capped with an honest `truncated` flag) and provenance {source_url, source, version}. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/docs/library with the required `ecosystem` (npm | pypi | crates | github; aliases pip/python, cargo/rust, node, gh accepted) and `name` (package name; for github use owner/repo like coinbase/x402), plus optional `version` (pin an exact version, default latest) and `topic` (a topic or symbol, e.g. 'authentication' or 'useEffect', matched against README/llms.txt headings). name: Agentstools Changelog
description: Returns the version-delta changelog for a library between two versions — the GitHub release notes in that range, the registry versions in between, and surfaced breaking-change markers — so a coding agent can decide whether an upgrade is safe. Keyless npm, PyPI, crates and GitHub sources; pay-per-call x402.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params, no request body. Required: ecosystem (string enum: npm | pypi | crates | github; aliases accepted — pip/python->pypi, cargo/rust->crates, node->npm, gh->github), name (string — package name; for github pass owner/repo such as coinbase/x402; npm scoped names @scope/name allowed), from_version (string — lower-bound version, e.g. 18.0.0, exclusive), to_version (string — upper-bound version, e.g. 19.0.0, inclusive).
backends.outputSchema: { found (bool), identity {ecosystem, name, latest_version, requested_version (null), resolved_version, license (SPDX), repository, homepage, documentation, source, versions[] (recent version strings), versions_count (int)}, from_version, to_version, versions_between[] (registry versions in the range), releases[] {version, name, published_at, url, prerelease (bool), notes (markdown release notes, byte-capped), notes_truncated (bool), breaking_markers[] (matched terms e.g. 'breaking change','deprecat','removed','no longer'), has_breaking (bool)}, release_count (int), breaking_changes[] (versions flagged breaking), available (bool), repository, license (SPDX), license_note (string — minimal cited slices only, whole docs never rehosted), attribution[] (per-source registry attribution) }.

Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). NOTE: the 402 quote is delivered in the base64 `payment-required` response HEADER; the 402 body is a bare {}.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. Check `found`, then read `identity` (resolved package: ecosystem, name, latest_version, resolved_version, license, repository, homepage, versions[], versions_count) and the delta fields: `versions_between[]` (registry versions in the range), `releases[]` (each with version, name, published_at, url, prerelease, notes (markdown release notes, byte-capped with an honest `notes_truncated` flag), breaking_markers[] and has_breaking), `release_count`, `breaking_changes[]` (versions flagged as breaking), and `available`. Top-level also carries license, license_note and attribution[]. Verified 2026-08-07 with {ecosystem:'npm', name:'react', from_version:'18.0.0', to_version:'19.0.0'} -> HTTP 200: found:true, identity resolved to react 19.2.8 (MIT, repo react/react), versions_between ['18.1.0','18.2.0','18.3.0','18.3.1','19.0.0'], release_count 5, breaking_changes ['v18.3.0','v19.0.0'] (v19.0.0 notes truncated at +7376 chars), $0.008 charged on Base.

from_version is exclusive and to_version is inclusive of the range (observed: from 18.0.0 to 19.0.0 returned versions_between starting at 18.1.0 and ending at 19.0.0).

Release notes are the raw GitHub release-notes markdown, byte-capped per release with an honest `notes_truncated` flag (v19.0.0's notes came back truncated at +7376 chars); breaking_markers[]/has_breaking are heuristic term matches ('breaking change','deprecat','removed','no longer').
Metadata + minimal provenance-cited slices only — whole documents are never rehosted; robots respected, no paywall bypass (see license_note). Keyless registries: npm, PyPI, crates.io, GitHub.

Flat price $0.008 USDC on Base only (amount 8000 atomic, USDC 6 decimals); no Solana leg, not a dynamic ceiling. The x402 quote lives in the base64 `payment-required` response HEADER, not the JSON body (402 body is a bare {}).

usage.guide: Decide whether upgrading a library between two versions is safe by reading the actual changelog. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/docs/changelog with all four required query params: `ecosystem` (npm | pypi | crates | github; aliases pip/python, cargo/rust, node, gh accepted), `name` (package name; for github use owner/repo like coinbase/x402), `from_version` (lower bound, exclusive, e.g. 18.0.0) and `to_version` (upper bound, inclusive, e.g. 19.0.0).
